scenes.title: The Magic Hidden Inside
narration: Have you ever wondered how a tiny mustard seed turns into a big plant?
Deep inside every seed is a tiny baby plant waiting for the right moment.
It needs a cozy home in the soil to start its amazing journey.

scenes.title: Steps to Wake Up
narration: First, the seed drinks up rainwater from the soil to wake up.
Then, the hard outer shell splits open to let the tiny roots out.
This process of a seed starting to grow is called germination.

scenes.title: Watching a Moong Sprout
narration: Let us watch a moong dal seed sprout in a wet cloth.
Day one, the seed swells up because it is full of water.
Day two, a white root pops out and pushes down into the dark.
Day three, a tiny green shoot reaches up to find the sunlight.

scenes.title: What We Learned
narration: Seeds need water, air, and warmth to grow into strong plants.
Germination is the start of a plant's exciting life cycle.
If you planted a seed today, what do you think it needs most?

scenes.title: The Big Question
narration: Have you seen Rohan's pet fish swimming happily in the water at home?
Why does a camel walk easily across the hot sand in the Thar Desert?
Animals have special body parts called adaptations that help them live in their homes.

scenes.title: Understanding Adaptations
narration: An adaptation is a special skill or body feature that helps an animal survive.
Some animals have thick fur to stay warm in the freezing Himalayan mountains.
Others have sharp claws to hunt or climb trees to find food.
These features make it possible for them to find food and stay safe.

scenes.title: The Desert Camel Example
narration: Let us look at the camel living in the dry Rajasthan desert.
It has wide, padded feet so it does not sink into the soft sand.
The hump stores fat so it can go many days without eating food.
These features keep the camel healthy even when it is very hot.

scenes.title: Recap and Challenge
narration: Adaptations are body parts or behaviors that help animals live in their environment.
From thick fur to wide feet, every animal is built for its home.
Think about it: what adaptation helps a frog jump high away from danger?

scenes.title: The Big Garden Mystery
narration: Look at Rohan's garden in Delhi, where birds, insects, and plants all live together.
Have you ever wondered how they all survive in the same small space?
They are part of an ecosystem, a big family that helps each other live.

scenes.title: How the System Works
narration: Every ecosystem has living things like trees, animals, and tiny bugs.
They also need non-living things like sunlight, water, and soil to stay healthy.
Plants use sunlight to make food, which then feeds the animals in the park.
When they pass away, they turn back into soil to help new plants grow.

scenes.title: A Pond Example
narration: Let us look at a pond near the village market.
Small fish eat the green algae growing in the water.
A kingfisher bird then catches the fish for its meal.
The water and sunlight keep the algae alive for the fish.

scenes.title: Keeping Our World Healthy
narration: Everything in an ecosystem is connected like a giant, beautiful puzzle.
If one piece is missing, the whole puzzle changes for everyone.
Think about it: what would happen to the garden if we took away all the bees?

scenes.title: The Garden Mystery
narration: Have you ever wondered how a tiny mango seed grows into a big tree?
Plants cannot walk, so they need a clever way to make new plant babies.
It all starts with a beautiful flower in our garden.

scenes.title: Parts of the Flower
narration: Flowers have special dust called pollen made in the stamen.
The pistil is the part that catches the pollen to start growing seeds.
This process of moving pollen is called pollination.

scenes.title: A Mango's Journey
narration: A busy bee lands on a mango flower to drink sweet nectar.
Sticky pollen gets stuck on the bee's fuzzy legs.
When the bee visits another flower, it leaves the pollen behind.
The flower then turns into a delicious, juicy mango fruit.

scenes.title: Wrapping It Up
narration: Pollination uses bees, wind, or butterflies to move pollen between flowers.
Once pollinated, the flower makes seeds that grow into new plants.
Think about it, what other animals help move pollen in your backyard?

scenes.title: The Meadow Mystery
narration: Have you ever wondered why grass grows and why birds hunt for worms?
Every living thing needs energy to play, grow, and move around.
Plants and animals are connected by what they eat in a food chain.

scenes.title: Steps Of The Chain
narration: Plants are producers because they make their own food using sunlight.
Animals are consumers because they must eat plants or other animals.
Decomposers like tiny fungi break down dead things to feed the soil.

scenes.title: A Garden Example
narration: In a garden, the Sun helps grass grow strong and healthy.
A hungry grasshopper eats the green grass for its lunch.
Then, a small garden frog hops over to eat the grasshopper.
Finally, a snake might come along to catch the frog.

scenes.title: Wrapping It Up
narration: Food chains always start with energy from the Sun.
Each step passes energy along to the next living creature.
Think about it: what would happen to the chain if plants disappeared?

scenes.title: A Yummy Snack Break
narration: Ananya is eating a crunchy apple at school, but where does that food go?
Have you ever wondered how your body turns an apple into energy for playing?
It all happens inside your amazing digestive system.

scenes.title: The Journey Begins
narration: It starts in your mouth where your teeth crush the food into tiny pieces.
Then, your spit mixes with the food to soften it up for the trip down.
Your food travels down a long tube into your stomach like a slide.

scenes.title: Inside the Belly
narration: In your stomach, juices break the apple down into a thick, soupy mix.
Next, it moves to the small intestine where nutrients soak into your blood.
Finally, your body takes out the water and gets rid of the waste parts.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: Digestion breaks down food into fuel so you can run, jump, and learn.
Remember, your mouth, stomach, and intestines work together as a super team.
Think about it: why is it important to chew your food very slowly?

scenes.title: The Big Breath Hook
narration: Have you ever wondered what happens when you take a deep breath after running?
Your chest rises and falls, but where does that air actually go inside you?
Let us explore the amazing path air takes to keep your body working.

scenes.title: The Path of Air
narration: Air enters through your nose or mouth, like when you sniff a jasmine flower.
It travels down a long tube called the windpipe into your chest.
Finally, the air fills up two soft, balloon-like organs called lungs.
Inside the lungs, your body grabs the oxygen it needs to stay strong.

scenes.title: Example: Playing Cricket
narration: Imagine Rohan is running fast to catch a cricket ball in the field.
His muscles need lots of oxygen, so his lungs work faster than usual.
He breathes out carbon dioxide, which is the air his body does not want.

scenes.title: Wrapping Up
narration: We breathe in oxygen to help us grow and breathe out carbon dioxide.
Your lungs are like busy engines that never stop working for you.
Think about it: Why do you think your breathing gets faster after exercise?

scenes.title: The Heart's Busy Job
narration: Have you ever felt your chest thumping after a fast race in the park?
That thumping is your heart working hard to keep you moving.
But what exactly is your heart doing inside your body?

scenes.title: Blood's Big Journey
narration: Your heart acts like a powerful pump for your blood.
Blood travels through tiny tubes called veins and arteries.
It carries fresh oxygen from your lungs to every single part of you.
It also picks up waste to take away so you stay healthy.

scenes.title: An Example of Flow
narration: Think of blood like a delivery truck bringing a parcel to your house.
The parcel is oxygen, and your house is your hungry toe.
Once the oxygen is dropped off, the truck picks up old trash to leave.
The cycle repeats over and over, thousands of times a day.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: So, your heart pumps blood through vessels to deliver oxygen everywhere.
It is a non-stop delivery service that keeps your whole body working.
Think about it: If your heart stopped pumping for a minute, what would happen?

Force.title: The Magic of Push and Pull

scenes.title: What Makes Things Move
narration: Have you ever wondered why your football rolls across the school field?
Everything needs a little help to start moving or stop moving.
That help is called a force.

scenes.title: Push or Pull
narration: You use a push to move something away from you.
Like pushing a heavy grocery cart at the local bazaar.
A pull brings something closer to you.
Think of opening a heavy door to your classroom.

scenes.title: Example in Action
narration: Let us see force in action with a game of tug-of-war.
When Rohan pulls the rope, the force moves it his way.
When Priya pulls harder, the rope moves toward her side.
The rope moves because force changes its position.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: Force is simply a push or a pull on an object.
Forces make things move, stop, or change direction.
Think about it: can you find three things in your house you push today?

scenes.title: The Daily Motion Hook
narration: Look at Rohan riding his bicycle to school through the market.
His wheels spin round and round to make him move forward.
Have you ever wondered what actually makes things start or stop moving?

scenes.title: Understanding Forces
narration: To move something, you need a force like a push or a pull.
A push moves an object away from you, like kicking a football.
A pull brings an object closer, like opening a heavy door.
Forces change how fast or in what direction things travel.

scenes.title: A Real Life Example
narration: Imagine Priya playing with her toy cart filled with mangoes.
She uses a strong push to make the heavy cart roll forward.
If she wants it to stop, she pulls back on the handle gently.
The cart moves because of the force Priya applies with her hands.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Motion is simply a change in position caused by pushes or pulls.
Remember, forces are needed to start, speed up, or stop movement.
Think about it: Can you name one thing you pushed today?

scenes.title: The Body's Hidden Support
narration: Have you ever wondered how Arjun stands tall without wobbling like a bowl of jelly?
It is all thanks to a strong, hidden frame inside you called the skeleton.
Without these bones, you would just be a heap on the floor!

scenes.title: What Bones Do For Us
narration: Your bones act like a hard helmet to protect your soft brain inside your head.
They also work with your muscles to help you run, jump, and play cricket.
Inside your long bones, your body even makes tiny parts for your blood.

scenes.title: How Many Bones?
narration: When you were a tiny baby, you had over three hundred squishy bones.
As you grow, some of those bones join together to become one solid piece.
Now, as a big kid, you have exactly two hundred and six bones.

scenes.title: Keep Your Bones Strong
narration: Drink milk and play in the sun to keep your bones hard and healthy.
Your skeleton is a wonderful, living, and growing part of you every single day.
Think about it: which bone in your body do you think is the longest one?

scenes.title: The Power in Everything
narration: Have you ever wondered how your toy car moves or how you run so fast?
It happens because of something invisible called energy.
Energy is simply the ability to do work or make things change.

scenes.title: Different Types of Energy
narration: Energy comes in many forms, like the heat from your morning chai.
Moving things, like a spinning ceiling fan, have kinetic energy.
Even a battery holds stored energy waiting to be used.
Light from the sun gives energy to plants so they can grow.

scenes.title: Energy at Home
narration: Think of Rohan eating a healthy banana before his football match.
His body changes the food into energy to kick the ball.
The ball moves because the energy was pushed into it.

scenes.title: Remembering Energy
narration: Energy can change forms, but it never disappears.
Without energy, nothing in the universe would ever move.
Think about it: What energy do you use to ride your bicycle to school?

scenes.title: A Sunny Surprise
narration: Have you ever wondered why your room is dark when you turn off the switch?
Light is energy that travels in a straight line from a source.
Without light, our eyes cannot see anything around us.

scenes.title: How Light Moves
narration: Light travels from a source like the Sun or a bulb.
It hits an object and bounces off it.
This bounce is called reflection, which brings light to our eyes.
Some objects are shiny like a mirror and reflect light perfectly.

scenes.title: Rohan's Shiny Spoon
narration: Rohan holds his steel spoon under the bright kitchen light.
The light hits the curved metal surface of the spoon.
The light bounces back, and Rohan sees his funny reflection.

scenes.title: Light Recap
narration: Light comes from a source and travels in straight lines.
When light hits an object, it reflects back to our eyes.
Think about it: why do you think we see colors in light?

scenes.title: The Everyday Mystery
narration: Have you ever wondered why your cricket ball always lands back on the ground?
Whether you drop a banana peel or jump up high, you always come back down.
Why don't we just float away into the blue sky like a loose balloon?

scenes.title: Meet Gravity
narration: There is an invisible force called gravity that pulls everything toward the center of Earth.
Think of Earth like a giant magnet that pulls on all objects, big or small.
The bigger an object is, the stronger its pull on things nearby.

scenes.title: Gravity in Action
narration: Imagine Priya drops her heavy school bag and a light paper sheet together.
Without air to slow it down, both would hit the ground at the same time.
Gravity works on everything, keeping our feet firmly on the park grass.

scenes.title: Gravity Recap
narration: Gravity is the invisible force pulling us toward the Earth's center every single day.
Without it, our homes, cars, and even our tea would float away into space.
Think about it, what would life be like if you could jump and never come down?

Muscular System.title: How Your Muscles Help You Move

scenes.title: The Power in Your Body
narration: Have you ever wondered how Rohan kicks his football so high across the park?
Inside your body, amazing elastic bands called muscles make all that movement happen.
Today we will see how your muscles pull your bones to get you moving.

scenes.title: How Muscles Work
narration: Muscles work in pairs to pull your bones in different directions.
When one muscle gets short and thick, it is called a contraction.
Then the other muscle relaxes and gets long to let the arm move back.
It is like a team effort where one pulls while the other waits.

scenes.title: Bending Your Arm
narration: Let us look at your bicep muscle when you lift your heavy school bag.
The bicep at the front tightens and pulls your forearm bone up.
At the same time, the tricep muscle at the back relaxes to let it happen.

scenes.title: Recap and Challenge
narration: Muscles are the strong bands that pull on your bones to create movement.
They always work in pairs by contracting and relaxing to bend your joints.
Think about it: which muscles do you think you use when you chew your lunch?

scenes.title: The Mystery of Sound
narration: Have you ever wondered how your friend's voice reaches your ears across the playground?
Ananya is hitting a plastic ruler on her desk at school.
Look closely, the ruler is moving back and forth very quickly.

scenes.title: Invisible Waves
narration: This quick movement is called a vibration.
Vibrations push the air around them to make invisible waves.
These waves travel through the air like ripples in a pond.
Sound can even travel through water or solid wood.

scenes.title: Hearing the Drum
narration: Imagine you are playing a small tabla drum at home.
When you strike the skin, it vibrates rapidly.
The air waves hit your ear and make your eardrum wiggle.
Your brain turns those wiggles into the sound of music.

scenes.title: Quick Sound Recap
narration: Sound starts with a vibration that pushes air waves.
These waves travel to your ears to create what you hear.
Think about it: Can you feel the vibration if you touch a speaker while music plays?

scenes.title: The Magic of Switches
narration: Have you ever wondered why the light turns on when you flip a switch at home?
It happens because electricity travels through wires like water through a pipe.
Let's discover how this invisible energy gets to your favorite toys.

scenes.title: The Electric Path
narration: Electricity needs a complete path called a circuit to move around.
Tiny particles called electrons zoom through the metal wires inside your walls.
If the path is broken, the electricity stops, and your bulb turns off.

scenes.title: Powering a Toy Car
narration: Think of a battery as a backpack full of energy for your toy car.
When you switch it on, electrons flow from the battery into the motor.
The motor turns, the wheels spin, and your car zooms across the floor!

scenes.title: Remembering the Basics
narration: Electricity is energy flowing in a closed loop called a circuit.
Switches act like gates that open or close the path for energy.
Think about it: what other things in your house need electricity to work?

scenes.title: Where are the magnets?
narration: Have you ever seen a fridge door stay shut all by itself?
A hidden magnet is pulling the door tight so it does not swing open.
How do these mysterious objects pull things without even touching them?

scenes.title: Understanding Magnetic Force
narration: Magnets have an invisible area around them called a magnetic field.
This field acts like a secret hand that reaches out to grab metal objects.
Magnets have two ends called poles, the North pole and the South pole.
Opposite poles pull together, but the same poles will push each other away.

scenes.title: Testing at Home
narration: Let us test some items in your kitchen with a magnet.
If you hold a magnet near a steel spoon, it snaps right onto it.
But if you try it on a plastic cup, nothing happens at all.
Magnets only stick to certain metals like iron or steel.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Magnets use invisible fields to pull or push magnetic objects.
Remember, opposite poles attract while matching poles push away.
Think about it: can you find three things in your classroom that magnets stick to?

scenes.title: Where Does Rain Come From?
narration: Have you ever wondered where rain comes from during our monsoon season?
Water doesn't just appear; it travels in a never-ending circle.
Let's follow a drop of water from a puddle in Delhi.

scenes.title: Evaporation and Condensation
narration: The hot sun heats up the puddle and turns water into invisible gas.
This rising gas cools down high up to form fluffy clouds.
Tiny water droplets gather together inside the cloud until it gets heavy.

scenes.title: Rainfall and Collection
narration: When the cloud is too full, it releases the water as rain.
The rain flows down from the Himalayas into the holy river Ganga.
Finally, the water collects back into a puddle to start again.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Water evaporates, turns into clouds, rains down, and collects again.
This cycle keeps our plants and trees green all year long.
Think about it: where would the water go if the sun stopped shining?

scenes.title: The Hidden World Beneath
narration: Have you ever wondered what is inside the mud in your garden?
Digging deep reveals more than just dirt for your marigolds.
Let us explore why soil is like a home for plants.

scenes.title: What Makes Soil
narration: Soil is a mix of tiny broken rocks and old dead leaves.
It also holds tiny air pockets and water for roots to drink.
Tiny bugs like earthworms help turn this into healthy food.

scenes.title: A Recipe for Growth
narration: Think of a pot in your kitchen holding mango saplings.
First, the roots push through the loose soil to find water.
Next, the rich nutrients from compost help the leaves turn green.
Finally, the soil holds the plant steady against the strong wind.

scenes.title: Soil is Precious
narration: Soil is made of rocks, water, air, and tiny living things.
Without good soil, our food would not be able to grow.
Think about it: how many different bugs can you find in your school garden?

scenes.title: What is stuff made of?
narration: Look at your water bottle and your sandwich, everything is made of matter.
Matter is simply anything that takes up space and has weight.
Have you ever wondered why ice turns into liquid water in your glass?

scenes.title: The Three States
narration: Solids like a brick stay in one shape.
Liquids like milk flow and take the shape of the container.
Gases like the air in a balloon spread out everywhere.

scenes.title: Watching Ice Melt
narration: Imagine an ice cube from your freezer on a hot Delhi afternoon.
As the ice gets warmer, it absorbs heat energy.
The solid ice melts and turns into liquid water.
If you boiled that water, it would become steam or gas.

scenes.title: Quick Review
narration: Matter exists as solid, liquid, or gas.
Adding heat can change matter from solid to liquid to gas.
Think about it: what happens to your ice cream if you leave it in the sun?

scenes.title: The World Around Us
narration: Look around your home in Mumbai, what do you see that nature gave us?
From the sunlight to the water in your tap, these are natural resources.
Have you ever wondered where all these things actually come from?

scenes.title: What Are Natural Resources?
narration: Natural resources are materials found on Earth that humans use to survive.
We have renewable resources like the bright Sun that never runs out.
Then there are non-renewable ones like coal that take millions of years to form.

scenes.title: Using Water Wisely
narration: Let us look at water, a precious resource we use for drinking and farming.
If we waste water while brushing our teeth, we have less for everyone else.
By turning off the tap, we ensure there is enough for the whole village.

scenes.title: Caring For Our Planet
narration: Remember, natural resources are limited, so we must use them carefully every day.
Recycle paper and save electricity to keep our Earth healthy and green.
What is one natural resource you can help save in your house today?

scenes.title: Finding Rocks Everywhere
narration: Have you ever wondered why the ground under your feet is so hard?
Whether you are playing in a park or walking to a shop, rocks are everywhere.
But did you know that rocks have their own secret life stories?

scenes.title: Three Types of Rocks
narration: Igneous rocks are born from hot, melted rock deep inside the Earth.
Sedimentary rocks form when tiny bits of sand and mud get squashed together.
Metamorphic rocks change shape because of intense heat and pressure underground.

scenes.title: A Story of Sandstone
narration: Let us look at a piece of red sandstone like those in Delhi forts.
First, tiny grains of sand settle at the bottom of a riverbed.
Over many years, weight from above pushes them into a solid rock.
Finally, the layers harden to become the beautiful stone we see today.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Rocks
narration: Rocks change through fire, pressure, and time in a never-ending cycle.
They can be igneous, sedimentary, or metamorphic, each with its own special look.
Think about it: can you find three different looking rocks in your garden today?

scenes.title: The Magic of Resources
narration: Have you ever wondered where the water for your morning bath comes from?
Everything we use, like electricity and paper, comes from nature.
But what happens if we use up all these gifts too quickly?

scenes.title: Understanding Conservation
narration: Conservation means using our resources wisely so they last a long time.
Think of it like your piggy bank filled with 500 rupees.
If you spend it all today, you will have nothing left tomorrow.
Saving small amounts helps you have money when you really need it.

scenes.title: Saving at Home
narration: At home, we can turn off the tap while brushing our teeth.
We can also turn off lights when leaving an empty room.
And we can recycle old notebooks instead of throwing them away.

scenes.title: Making a Big Difference
narration: Conservation is protecting our planet by using less and reusing more.
Every small action you take helps keep India green and beautiful.
Think about it: what is one thing you can save today?

scenes.title: What Is Pollution?
narration: Look at the busy streets of Mumbai, do you see the grey smoke from cars?
That dirty air and trash in our parks is called pollution.
Why is it harmful to our beautiful planet?

scenes.title: How Pollution Spreads
narration: Pollution happens when we add bad things to nature like plastic or oil.
Smoke from factories rises high and mixes with the clean air.
Plastic thrown in our rivers flows into the deep blue sea.
This makes it hard for animals and plants to stay healthy.

scenes.title: See It In Action
narration: Imagine you drop a plastic bottle near the Ganga river.
The water carries the bottle far away to the ocean.
A fish might think it is food and try to eat it.
This shows how one small piece of trash causes a big problem.

scenes.title: We Can Help
narration: We can stop pollution by using less plastic and recycling our waste.
Remember to pick up trash and keep our neighborhood clean.
Think about it: what is one thing you can recycle today?
